evals.prompt: Use the connector-bootstrap skill. I have two Plane workspaces connected: one self-hosted and one cloud. Show me the backlog. Describe how you find the tools, what you notice about having two connections, and what you do before touching either instance. If you can't run it here, show me the exact calls you would make, in order, and what they return. Keep it short.
evals.expected_output: Agent detects multiple Plane instances from ToolSearch results and asks which one to use before listing anything.
expectations: The answer says to probe ToolSearch and finds workitem or cycle resource tool(s), or list_work_items on a legacy connector
The answer says that two connections expose tools with the same resource or action names under different server segments
The answer asks the user which instance to operate on instead of guessing
The answer says to remember the choice for subsequent calls in the session

evals.prompt: Use the connector-bootstrap skill. I don't have Plane set up. Tell me I don't have Plane tools. If you can't run it here, show me the exact calls you would make, in order, and what they return.
evals.expected_output: Agent probes ToolSearch at least 4 times across relevant domains before concluding Plane is not connected, and reports which probes were run.
expectations: The answer says to run at least 4 distinct ToolSearch queries before refusing
The answer lists the exact probes it ran (or would run) in the refusal message
The answer suggests how to connect Plane (MCP, connector, or cowork mode)
The answer does not silently refuse without probing

evals.prompt: Use the connector-bootstrap skill. We run Plane on our own server and want Claude Code to work with it from a CI job, with nobody there to log in through a browser. Plane tools are not connected yet. How do I connect it? If you can't run it here, show me the exact calls you would make, in order, and what they return.
evals.expected_output: Self-hosted headless setup: stdio server with the three environment variables, a connection name containing plane, and the limits of the hosted server.
expectations: The answer connects the self-hosted instance with uvx plane-mcp-server stdio
The answer says to set PLANE_BASE_URL to the self-hosted URL
The answer says to set PLANE_API_KEY and PLANE_WORKSPACE_SLUG
The answer says the hosted server at mcp.plane.so cannot reach a private self-hosted instance
The answer says to name the connection with plane in its name, because the safety hook only watches servers whose name contains plane
The answer does not use the deprecated SSE endpoint or the npm package @makeplane/plane-mcp-server

evals.prompt: Use the connector-bootstrap skill. What's the weather in Berlin tomorrow? If you can't run it here, show me the exact calls you would make, in order, and what they return.
evals.expected_output: Agent does NOT trigger connector-bootstrap — this is unrelated to work management.
expectations: The answer does not claim to have found or called any Plane tool
The answer does not load the connector-bootstrap skill content
The answer answers the weather question normally or explains it lacks weather data

evals.prompt: Use the connector-bootstrap skill. Plane MCP 0.3.3 is connected. My call workitem(action=retrieve, project_id=<id>, work_item_id=<id>) was rejected as invalid. Fix the call. Afterwards I want PROJ-9 deleted: tell me what happens when you call delete and what you do if I decline the dialog. Also tell me what you do when the corrected call is rejected again. If you can't run it here, show me the exact calls you would make, in order, and what they return. Keep it short.
evals.expected_output: Corrected call with workitem_id, the declared-parameters rule, and the delete behavior of the safety hook.
expectations: The answer says the id of a work item is workitem_id, not work_item_id
The answer says the parameters are validated against the declared set of the action, so an extra or misspelled parameter is an error
The answer says to re-read the tool description of the action before retrying instead of guessing
The answer says a delete action shows the Claude Code permission dialog because of the plugin's PreToolUse hook
The answer says to tell the user which work item will be deleted before it calls delete
The answer does not retry a delete that the user declined

evals.prompt: Use the connector-bootstrap skill. Create an epic 'Checkout redesign' in project TaskFlow and attach it to the initiative 'Q4 Growth'. Say which tool names you look for and give the full call sequence with parameters. If you can't run it here, show me the exact calls you would make, in order, and what they return.
evals.expected_output: Agent knows that no epic tools exist: resolves the Epic work item type, creates a workitem with that type_id, then attaches it with initiative(action=manage_workitems, add_ids=[...]).
expectations: The answer does not search for or call create_epic / add_epic_to_initiative
The answer says to call workitem_type(action=resolve, name='Epic') to get the type_id
The answer says to create the epic with workitem(action=create) and the type_id of the Epic type
The answer says to attach the epic to the initiative with initiative(action=manage_workitems) and add_ids

evals.prompt: Use the connector-bootstrap skill. Add PROJ-148 and PROJ-150 to the Sprint 15 cycle of TaskFlow. This Plane connector is an old one: ToolSearch only shows list_cycles, create_cycle, list_work_items, add_work_items_to_cycle and similar per-operation tools; there is no workitem or cycle tool. Show each call with its parameters, how you resolve the two identifiers, and what you tell me about this connector. Also tell me whether pql filters and counts work on this connector. If you can't run it here, show me the exact calls you would make, in order, and what they return. Keep it short.
evals.expected_output: Agent recognizes the per-operation surface, uses the fallback table to translate cycle(action=manage_workitems, add_ids=[...]) into the connector's add_work_items_to_cycle with issue_ids, and checks the schema for parameter names first.
expectations: The answer identifies the connector as the per-operation fallback surface (no workitem or cycle tool, no action parameter)
The answer translates cycle(action=manage_workitems, add_ids=[...]) into add_work_items_to_cycle
The answer says to pass the work item ids as issue_ids
The answer says to resolve PROJ-148 with retrieve_work_item_by_identifier, project_identifier="PROJ" and the integer issue_identifier=148
The answer recommends upgrading the server to Plane MCP 0.3.0 or later
The answer says that pql and count are unavailable on this connector

evals.prompt: Use the connector-bootstrap skill. Which work items are overdue and still open across all our Plane projects? We run Plane MCP 0.3.3. Show the exact call including its filter, how you find the tool, and how you handle a long result. If you can't run it here, show me the exact calls you would make, in order, and what they return. Keep it short.
evals.expected_output: Agent finds the resource surface and uses a server-side PQL filter on workitem list without a project_id, instead of looping over projects and filtering client-side.
expectations: The answer says to probe ToolSearch with the queries plane and workitem cycle module
The answer says to call workitem(action=list) with a pql filter and without project_id to search the whole workspace
The answer says to call get_pql_reference for the filter syntax and mentions the limit of 5 conditions
The answer says to follow next_cursor if the result is paginated
